objective: Move software toward or through an operational change safely, with environment evidence, explicit rollback, authorization-aware execution, and write-time target revalidation.

stages.purpose: Identify the target environment, current deployed/runtime state and revision, CI/CD path, configuration, dependencies, authorization boundary, and whether the current execution environment can actually reach the authorized target.
evidence: explicit unknown state when direct evidence cannot be obtained
stages.exit_when: The system knows the target environment, the allowed access path, the current material target revision/state, whether that path is usable from the current execution context, and which facts remain unknown.

stages.purpose: If execution is actually reachable and authorized, define preflight checks, expected target revision/preconditions, failure thresholds, rollback or restore path, and any required user authorization before writes; otherwise record the blocker and minimal unblock condition without widening access.
evidence: expected target revision/resource version when supported
or a bounded blocker record when the route cannot proceed
stages.exit_when: The change can be attempted against an explicit current target/precondition with bounded blast radius and recovery, or the exact blocker/minimal unblock is recorded and execution stops safely.

stages.purpose: Revalidate the material target precondition immediately before the authorized operational write, reconcile or stop if the target moved, then perform only the authorized change/read-only verification and validate target behavior against acceptance and rollback thresholds. Never infer production facts from repository/local evidence when target evidence is unavailable.
evidence: or explicit not-executed/revalidation-required status when blocked or moved
stages.exit_when: The operational objective is reached and healthy, rollback restored a known-good state, or execution stopped/replanned safely because authorization, reachability, or the validated target baseline no longer held.

pressure_guards.rule: Before the first material mutation in an existing project or target environment, reconcile the current implementation/runtime baseline with the project-defined authority and freshness of material state, specification, test, adapter, deployment, and historical evidence. A failing test can itself encode a stale historical assumption; classify that possibility before changing product or operational behavior. Preserve material conflicts and keep unknown facts unknown rather than silently converting them to false/absent state.

When a custom test runner, CI wrapper, validation aggregator, generated report, or similar harness materially converts underlying checks into pass/fail acceptance evidence, do not trust a green aggregate merely because the wrapper exited successfully. Verify the smallest consequential integrity surface: intended checks are discovered distinctly, collisions/cached reuse/duplicate counting do not substitute one check for another, skipped/errored/unavailable work is represented honestly, and failures propagate through wrapper exit/status semantics. If harness integrity is unknown or disproven, downgrade the aggregate to provisional/unknown evidence and use direct underlying checks or repair the harness before relying on it for regression, completion, or release claims.

A network policy, missing authorization, absent credential, inaccessible external system, required product decision, or stale/moved target precondition is a blocker/revalidation condition—not automatically a missing technical capability. Do not search for/install providers to bypass it unless an authorized capability gap genuinely exists.

When direct target evidence cannot be obtained, keep deployment/runtime facts unknown. Git state, CI success, local health, or guessed public behavior must not be promoted into verified target-environment facts.

Before a consequential merge, deployment, migration, configuration, data, or other operational write, revalidate the target revision/resource version/precondition used by preflight and use native conditional-write semantics when available. If the target moved, treat it as new evidence: do not force through the stale plan; re-read target state, preserve concurrent changes, recompute the operational delta and rollback/risk assumptions, re-check authorization if material, and execute only against the newly validated baseline.

escalations.when: Browser-visible smoke validation is required, the target is reachable/authorized, and the current release pipeline lacks a reliable check.
escalations.selection_rule: Prefer a durable Playwright smoke test when the check should repeat; use interactive agent browser control only when exploration is genuinely needed.

escalations.when: Release orchestration itself must become a durable structured workflow with explicit sessions, hosting, or typed workflow state.
escalations.selection_rule: Use a dedicated runtime only when the operational workflow is becoming a product/system in its own right, not for an ordinary application deploy.

escalations.when: Many humans/agents/runtimes need persistent approvals, permissions, audit, and scheduling for operations.
escalations.selection_rule: Treat this as Level 5 infrastructure and adopt only when shared governance is the actual requirement.

escalations.when: The project already uses Spec Kit and a reviewed release/ship extension closes a proven workflow gap.
escalations.selection_rule: Review community extension source/provenance/permissions before adoption; catalog presence alone is not trust.

verification: target environment identity and final state are explicit or intentionally unknown when direct evidence is blocked
preflight and post-change evidence are recorded when execution occurred

when a custom verification aggregator is material to release eligibility, its discovery/identity/failure-propagation integrity is credible enough for the release claim rather than assumed from a green wrapper result
rollback was defined before consequential writes
the material target revision/precondition was revalidated immediately before the operational write when practical
a moved target caused reconciliation/replanning rather than stale force execution
no production write exceeded the granted authorization scope
environment/authorization/concurrency blockers were not bypassed by unauthorized provider, network, force, or alternate write workarounds
reroute_signals: a code defect is blocking release -> bug-fix
a product behavior must change before release -> feature-change
the deployment repository/configuration is too contradictory to trust -> repo-recovery
a green release/CI aggregate is materially authoritative but its harness integrity is disproven -> repair the verification harness under bug-fix or use direct underlying checks before release
the target changed materially since preflight -> re-read/replan the current release delta before executing
